assumptions.condition: \(I_{\mathrm{cr}},I_{\mathrm{tr}},I_{\mathrm{va}}\) are a deterministic partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with positive cardinalities.

novel.justification: A finite predeclared list of target and critic architectures is realistic in a model-selection problem. It makes the simultaneous multiplicity penalty explicit without encoding a target rate.
A finite common audit sieve is implementable and permits a transparent validation concentration term. It does not impose a rate on the conditional-moment law.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal H_k\) is a compact convex subset of \(\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{kj}:1\le j\le d_{H,k}\}\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\).
For every \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(1\le j\le d_{H,k}\), \(g_{kj}\) is \(L_2(P_Z)\)-estimable from \(I_{\mathrm{cr}}\) at deterministic radius \(a_{k,n}\).
For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\{h_{k\ell}:\ell\ge1\}\subset\mathcal H_k\) is a fixed countable \(L_2(P_X)\)-dense subset containing \(0\).

novel.justification: Rational coefficient vectors give such an enumeration for every finite bounded sieve, including the two-coordinate diagnostic. It fixes a measurable optimization path without making an estimator property a model-membership condition.

This proposal-specific finite-grid condition merely reaches the displayed continuous oracle scale. For \(J_n=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\), it follows if \(s_{k,n}\ge 2^{-(1+\bar\beta)}n^{-(1+\bar\beta)}\) for every candidate.

definitions.name: Common-audit TRAE configuration class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n\) is the class of complete common-audit TRAE configurations \((P,I_{\mathrm{cr}},I_{\mathrm{tr}},I_{\mathrm{va}},\mathcal A_0,(\phi_{kj},J_k,\mathcal H_k,(h_{k\ell})_{\ell\ge1},\widehat g_{kj})_{k\in\mathcal K,1\le j\le d_{H,k}})\) satisfying \(\texttt{ass:iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:three-way-split}\), \(\texttt{ass:bounded-outcome}\), \(\texttt{ass:bounded-bases}\), \(\texttt{ass:finite-candidates}\), \(\texttt{ass:finite-audit}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-origin}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-compact-convex}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-coefficient-radius}\), \(\texttt{ass:image-estimability}\), \(\texttt{ass:pseudotrue-attainment}\), and \(\texttt{ass:dense-enumeration}\). The source conditions are theorem-side regularity conditions, not membership conditions, and no training-coverage, inverse-stability, or oracle-rate property is built into \(\mathcal M_n\).

definitions.name: Finite learned-image critic construction
definitions.construction: For each \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(1\le j\le d_{H,k}\), fit \(\widehat g_{kj}\) using only \(I_{\mathrm{cr}}\), set \(\alpha_{k,n}=\max_{1\le j\le d_{H,k}}\|\widehat g_{kj}-g_{kj}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}\), and set \(\widehat{\mathcal F}_k=\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_j\widehat g_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\}\).

definitions.name: Common ideal and learned audit classes
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}=\operatorname{absconv}(\mathcal A_0\cup\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_jg_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\})\), \(\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}=\operatorname{absconv}(\mathcal A_0\cup\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\widehat{\mathcal F}_k)\), \(D_{\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}(v)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}\{2E_P[v(Z)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\}\), \(\varepsilon_{H,k}=\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\|h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}\), and \(\varepsilon_{A,k}^2=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\{\|q_h-q_{h^\dagger}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2-D_{\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}(q_h-q_{h^\dagger})\}_+\).

definitions.name: Measurable common-audit TRAE selector and trained path
definitions.construction: For \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\lambda\in\Lambda_n\), and \(\ell\ge1\), let \(A_{k,\lambda,\ell}=\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}_k}\{2P_{\mathrm{tr}}[(Y-h_{k\ell}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{tr}}[f(Z)^2]\}+\lambda P_{\mathrm{tr}}[h_{k\ell}(X)^2]\). Let \(\widehat h_{k,\lambda}\) be the least-index \(h_{k\ell}\) whose score is within \(n^{-1}\) of \(\inf_{m\ge1}A_{k,\lambda,m}\), with index one as a deterministic fallback. Set \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}=\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}}\{2P_{\mathrm{va}}[(Y-\widehat h_{k,\lambda}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{va}}[f(Z)^2]\}\), \(\operatorname{pen}_n=8B^2\sqrt{\log(4K|\Lambda_n|/\eta)/n_{\mathrm{va}}}\), and let \((\widehat k,\widehat\lambda)\) be the lexicographically least minimizer of \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}+\operatorname{pen}_n\); finally set \(\widehat h=\widehat h_{\widehat k,\widehat\lambda}\). The selection stage is restricted to the finite trained path \(\{\widehat h_{k,\lambda}:k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n\}\). A path-restricted selector means any measurable map valued in that set, and a convex path aggregation means any convex combination of its elements; neither operation retrains a candidate.

definitions.name: Two-coordinate common-audit configuration
definitions.construction: Let \(U,V,\xi\) be mutually independent Rademacher variables, set \(X=Z=(U,V)\), \(h_0=w=a_0U+b_0V\), \(Y=a_0U+b_0V+\xi\), \(\mathcal K=\{1,2\}\), \(B=2\), and \(\mathcal H_1=\mathcal H_2=\{aU+bV:|a|+|b|\le2\}\). Use the common target basis \(\phi_{k1}=U,\phi_{k2}=V\), its rational-coefficient dense enumeration, \(J_1=\{1,2\}\), \(J_2=\{1\}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal F}_1=\{s\widehat g_{11}+t\widehat g_{12}:|s|+|t|\le2\}\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal F}_2=\{s\widehat g_{21}:|s|\le2\}\). Take \(\mathcal A_0=\{0\}\) and form \(\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}\) as in \(\texttt{def:common-audit}\).

definitions.name: Population training-coverage distance
definitions.construction:
For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), define the bounded training critic body
\[
 \mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}
 =\left\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_jg_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}^2
 =\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}
 \left\{
 \|q_h-q_{h^\dagger}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2
 -\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}}
 \left(2E_P[(q_h-q_{h^\dagger})(Z)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\right)
 \right\}.
\]
Equivalently, as proved in \(\texttt{lem:training-coverage-distance-identity}\),
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}^2
 =\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}
 \operatorname{dist}_{L_2(P_Z)}^2
 \bigl(q_h-q_{h^\dagger},\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}\bigr).
\]
The inner dual problem is a finite-dimensional concave quadratic optimization over an \(\ell_1\)-ball, and the outer problem is over the compact coefficient set defining \(\mathcal H_k\). The relevant geometry is the compact bounded critic body itself, not merely its linear span.

definitions.name: Constant-target two-atom common-audit configuration
definitions.construction: Fix \(B>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), and put \(a=B\sqrt{\gamma}\). Let \(X=Z\in\{-1,1\}\) with \(P(X=Z=1)=p\in(0,1)\), let \(Y=a\) almost surely, and write \(\mathbf 1\) for the constant-one function. Set \(h_0=w=a\mathbf 1\), \(\mathcal K=\{1,2\}\), \(d_{H,1}=d_{H,2}=1\), \(\phi_{11}=\phi_{21}=\mathbf 1\), \(\mathcal H_1=\{0\}\), and \(\mathcal H_2=\{c\mathbf 1:0\le c\le a\}\). Take \(J_1=\{1\}\), \(J_2=\varnothing\), set \(\widehat g_{11}=\widehat g_{21}=\mathbf 1\) and \(a_{1,n}=a_{2,n}=0\), enumerate \(\mathcal H_1\) by zero and enumerate a countable dense subset of \(\mathcal H_2\) with \(h_{21}=0\), and set \(\mathcal A_0=\{0\}\). Form the learned training critics and common audit by \(\texttt{def:learned-images}\) and \(\texttt{def:common-audit}\). Along \(n=3m\), use any deterministic balanced three-way partition and set \(\eta=1/4\).

statements.justification: Conditional expectation is the basic stability inequality needed to separate target approximation from inverse amplification.
statements.gap: It is a standard Jensen reduction, not a claimed advance over prior work.
statements.consumer: It converts a target-sieve approximation into a weak-residual approximation in the oracle analysis.

statements.statement:
For any candidate \(k_0\), if \(0<s_{k_0,n}\le1\) and \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\) holds, then the deterministic grid functional satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
 \left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\frac{s_{k_0,n}}{\lambda}\right\}
 \le3s_{k_0,n}^{\bar\beta/(1+\bar\beta)}.
\]
This algebraic optimization does not imply a rate for \(\widehat h\) under \(\mathcal M_n\): \(\texttt{thm:common-audit-oracle-impossibility}\) gives zero-defect configurations for which the displayed functional converges to zero while \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2=1/32\) almost surely. Independently, that theorem gives the deterministic clipping bound \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2\). The grid exponent equals \(\beta/(1+\beta)\) for \(\beta\le1\) and saturates at \(1/2\) for \(\beta>1\).
statements.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Put \(a=\bar\beta\in(0,1]\), \(s=s_{k_0,n}\), and \(t=s^{1/(1+a)}\). Since \(0<s\le1\), one has \(0<t\le1\). By \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\),
\[
 2^{-J_n}\le \frac{t}{2}.
\]
Because \(\Lambda_n=\{2^{-j}:0\le j\le J_n\}\), there is a grid point \(\lambda_t\in\Lambda_n\) such that
\[
 \frac{t}{2}<\lambda_t\le t.
\]
Indeed, choose the largest dyadic grid point not exceeding \(t\). The lower endpoint of the grid is at most \(t/2\), and adjacent grid points differ by a factor of two. Therefore
\[
 \lambda_t^a+\frac{s}{\lambda_t}
 \le t^a+\frac{2s}{t}
 =s^{a/(1+a)}+2s^{a/(1+a)}
 =3s^{a/(1+a)}.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\lambda\in\Lambda_n\) proves
\[
 \inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
 \left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\frac{s_{k_0,n}}{\lambda}\right\}
 \le3s_{k_0,n}^{\bar\beta/(1+\bar\beta)}.
\]

This numerical inequality is not an estimator guarantee. Apply \(\texttt{thm:common-audit-oracle-impossibility}\) with \(B=2\), \(\gamma=1/128\), and \(\eta=1/4\). Then \(\gamma B^2=1/32\), candidate \(2\) satisfies
\[
 \varepsilon_{H,2}=\varepsilon_{A,2}=\alpha_{2,n}=0,
\]
the optimized grid functional converges to zero, and the selected estimator satisfies
\[
 \|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2=\frac{1}{32}
\]
for every sample. The same theorem gives the logically separate deterministic clipping bound
\[
 \|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2.
\]
Finally, if \(0<\beta\le1\), then \(a=\beta\) and \(a/(1+a)=\beta/(1+\beta)\). If \(1<\beta\le2\), then \(a=1\) and \(a/(1+a)=1/2\). This proves the asserted saturation statement.
\end{proof}
statements.justification: This proposition isolates the deterministic optimization supplied by the finite dyadic Tikhonov grid. For every candidate \(k_0\) satisfying \(0<s_{k_0,n}\le1\) and \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\), the grid contains a level within a factor of two of the continuous bias--variance balance, which yields the stated factor-three bound.
statements.gap: The calculation controls only the displayed grid functional and does not by itself control \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\). Zero benchmark defects are not premises of this proposition; they enter only in the later collapsed-path witness showing that the grid functional can vanish while the estimator's strong error remains positive.
statements.consumer: Use this proposition only to simplify the deterministic oracle expression and read off its saturation exponent. Any estimator-level conclusion additionally needs training-critic coverage or another argument linking the trained path to the pseudo-true target.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:iv-validity}\) and \(\texttt{ass:completeness}\), \(r=Th_0\) and \(h^\dagger=h_0\). Without those conditions, \(h^\dagger\) in \(\texttt{def:pseudotrue-target}\) is only a minimum-norm pseudo-true sensitivity target and is not automatically causal.
statements.justification: This proposition keeps the statistical inverse target distinct from the causal structural response.
statements.gap: Misspecified conditional moments identify a pseudo-true projection, not automatically \(h_0\).
statements.consumer: It tells applied users when the clipping and impossibility statements concern a causal response and when they concern only sensitivity to the observed conditional moment.

statements.statement: In \(\texttt{def:two-coordinate-configuration}\), \(T=I\), \(w=h_0=a_0U+b_0V\), and \(\alpha_{1,n}=\alpha_{2,n}=0\) when the learned images equal their ideal images. Under that ideal-image equality, candidate \(2\)'s critic is orthogonal to the \(V\) coordinate, and the population counterpart of its unpenalized training dual loss at the blind fit \(a_0U\) is exactly zero: \[\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}_2}\left\{2E_P[(Y-a_0U)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\right\}=0.\] Nevertheless, \(V\in\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}\) through candidate \(1\), and the common validation score at the blind fit has population counterpart satisfying \[\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}}\left\{2E_P[(Y-a_0U)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\right\}\ge b_0^2.\]
statements.justification: The bounded diagnostic shows at population level that the common audit assigns positive loss to a residual coordinate omitted by a candidate's own critic.
statements.gap: Detection by validation alone does not establish that any trained candidate path fits the detected coordinate.
statements.consumer: Together with the impossibility theorem, it separates the audit's diagnostic role from the training path's constructive role.

sampling_model.design: The general model uses independent draws from \(P\), deterministically split into positive-size critic-construction, training, and validation samples. The negative frontier uses balanced splits along \(n=3m\); the clipping-sharpness witness uses a positive-probability event on which training misses one support point.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X_i\) is endogenous in the general NPIV model and \(Z_i\) indexes the conditional moment. The diagnostic witnesses set \(X=Z\), so \(T=I\), only to isolate the path-selection obstruction from ill-posed inversion.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap premise is used. In the exact-frontier witness, \(X=Z\) takes two distinct values with probability \(1/2\) each for every \(\gamma\in(0,1]\). The parameter \(\gamma\) scales the constant target amplitude, not the support probabilities, so the endpoint \(\gamma=1\) preserves genuine two-atom support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite images \(g_{kj}=E_P[\phi_{kj}(X)\mid Z]\) are learned on the critic split. The counterexample grants exact images, so its failure is not a nuisance-estimation artifact. The remaining obstruction is candidate-level training coverage, measured by distance to \(\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.13 gives discrepancy-selected TRAE adaptive rates under target realizability and exact critic closeness, with saturation for \(\beta>1\).
Theorem 12 and Section 8 give misspecified RDIV bounds and validation model selection with target-class and learned-operator approximation terms.
Localized minimax conditional-moment analysis requires witness richness for projected residual control.
The paper studies fixed-tuning adversarial Tikhonov estimators under exact inverse equations for source-condition inference.

tldr: For the note-defined hybrid that combines candidate-specific adversarial training with a shared absolute-convex holdout audit, the paper proves the computable training-coverage distance identity, an exact nonzero collapsed-path failure frontier \((0,B^2]\) with attained endpoint \(B^2\), and failure of every signed or affine combination of an entirely collapsed trained path. Separately, it proves the deterministic envelope \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2\) with supremum-sharp coefficient \(4\). These are architecture-level diagnostics for the note-defined hybrid. Tan--Syrgkanis discrepancy-selected TRAE and Li--Lan--Syrgkanis--Wang--Uehara Regularized DeepIV are positive neighboring comparators, not workflows refuted by the theorem.

project_justification.gap: Tan and Syrgkanis prove positive discrepancy-selected TRAE rates under the assumptions of their Proposition 3.12, including critic-closeness or witness-coverage structure. Li, Lan, Syrgkanis, Wang, and Uehara use a different positive workflow in Section 8 and Algorithm 2: held-out Best-ERM or Convex-ERM compares candidates through a shared explicit learned-operator loss. Neither result studies the note-defined hybrid in which each candidate is trained against its own adversarial critic body and a common absolute-convex audit later selects only among the already-trained path. The paper therefore does not claim that either published workflow fails.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates a property of its own path-restricted hybrid: validation-time visibility of a residual direction is distinct from training-time coverage of that direction. The evaluable diagnostic is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}\), the worst distance from target-sieve residual differences to the compact bounded ideal training critic body \(\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}\).
project_justification.fill: The mathematical contribution is the training-coverage distance identity; a genuine two-atom exact-image witness with zero target, audit, and image defects; the exact attainable collapsed-path error frontier \((0,B^2]\); exhaustive failure of all random, data-dependent, or oracle-dependent signed and affine combinations of that collapsed path; and, independently, the supremum-sharp deterministic clipping constant \(4B^2\). The result diagnoses the note-defined hybrid only. A negative theorem about an accurately named published workflow would require a materially different construction and proof.

interpretation: The training-coverage identity says exactly what the note-defined hybrid can miss: membership in the linear span of available images is insufficient when a candidate trains against a bounded critic body. In the endpoint witness, the common audit contains the omitted constant residual and therefore can detect it, but both trained candidates are already zero. Selection, randomization, and even oracle-dependent signed or affine reweighting cannot create a function outside that collapsed path. The error equals \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},2}^2=\gamma B^2\), reaches \(B^2\) at \(\gamma=1\), and cannot exceed that endpoint for a collapsed-zero path under the source-radius condition. This mechanism is a diagnostic for the note-defined hybrid, not an interpretation of the algorithms in either cited positive comparator.
technical_internal_limitation: The negative theorem is architecture-specific. It covers the finite trained path generated by the note's candidate-specific adversarial critics and subsequently scored by its common audit, including every signed or affine combination of those already-trained elements. It does not cover refitting after validation, adding an audit-detected coordinate to training, imposing quantitative control of \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}\), Tan--Syrgkanis discrepancy-selected TRAE under its witness-coverage premises, or Li et al.'s shared explicit learned-operator Best-ERM and Convex-ERM workflow. The \(4B^2\) result is a sharp deterministic envelope rather than a convergence rate. A negative result about a named published workflow requires a different theorem whose estimator and assumptions reproduce that workflow accurately.
honest_scope: The formal theorem concerns only the common-audit selector defined in this note over finite bounded sieves, three deterministic sample splits, bounded outcomes and bases, and the stated Tikhonov source ball. Its two-atom witness grants exact learned images and zero declared benchmark defects, proves the exact \((0,B^2]\) collapsed-path frontier, and leaves retraining and richer critic construction outside scope. Tan--Syrgkanis and Li et al. are unmatched positive neighboring comparators and are not refuted. The statistical loss is centered at the minimum-norm pseudo-true response \(h^\dagger\); it concerns the causal response \(h_0\) only under the separate IV-validity and completeness assumptions.
